images.title: A transversal and eight angles
images.purpose: Show one line crossing two lines, the eight angles it makes, and the four equal pairs.
images.composition: One figure centred on the white canvas: two horizontal lines and one slanting line crossing both, with plenty of space around it.
exact_structure: Two horizontal grey (#6B7280) lines, l above and m below, equal length, not marked parallel.
One slanting dark line t crossing l and m, one crossing point on each line.
At the crossing with l, four small arcs numbered clockwise from the top left: 1 top left, 2 top right, 3 bottom right, 4 bottom left.
At the crossing with m, four small arcs numbered the same way: 5 top left, 6 top right, 7 bottom right, 8 bottom left.
Vertically opposite pairs share a colour: 1 and 3 teal (#0072B2), 2 and 4 amber (#E69F00), 5 and 7 green (#009E73), 6 and 8 reddish purple (#CC79A7).
Eight arcs in total, each with its number beside it; the lines are named l, m and t at their ends.
rejection: an opposite pair drawn in different colours
numbers placed so that 1 and 3 are not vertically opposite
images.takeaway: Eight angles, in four equal pairs, so at most four different sizes.
images.description: A line t crossing lines l and m with eight numbered angles in four colour-matched opposite pairs.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students find each colour pair and see why the eight angles cannot all differ.

image_decisions.why: One transversal figure shows the eight angles and the four equal pairs.
